title: Real exam maps
subtitle: 5 sets of map & plan vocabulary, each on a real exam-style map
source: Word lists and sentences: docs/listening_map_vocabulary_source.md. Map images: Cambridge English past papers (copyright Cambridge) — for private study only; replace before any public release.

sets.title: Inside a building
sets.focus: Simple prepositions of place: where one thing is compared with another.

words.meaning: directly ahead of something, on the side it faces
looking towards something; the front of one points at the other
in the centre, with space on all sides
at the back of something, on the side away from you
with one thing on each side
right beside it, touching or very close

sentences.text: The entrance is in front of the reception desk.
The reception desk is facing the entrance.
The pool is in the middle of the sports centre.
The gym is behind the swimming pool.
The pool is between the reception and the gym.
The seating area is next to the pool.

sets.title: Walking through a building
sets.focus: Sides and movement: left / right as you walk in, and going through or along.

words.meaning: on your left as you face forward or walk in
on your right as you face forward
go in one side and out the other (a door, gate or room)
change direction to your right
on the opposite side of a building, road or area
further on than something, past it
following the length of something (a corridor, wall or road)
where two walls or roads meet; ‘the far corner’ = the one furthest away
keep moving forward without turning
at the side of; next to
on your right from where you are standing or walking

sentences.text: The sports shop is on the left-hand side as you enter the sports centre.
To the right-hand side of the entrance, there's a café.
Pass through the entrance, turn right and the café is immediately in front of you.

The leisure pool is on the other side of the sports centre to the dance studios.

sentences.text: The houses immediately to the north and south of the Post Office are very near the river.
The bridge is just beyond the final row of houses heading north.
After crossing the bridge, take the second turning on the left and you'll see the retirement home straight ahead.
After crossing the bridge, take the second turning on the left and you'll see the retirement home straight ahead.

The retirement home is just southeast of the primary school.
The post office is to the northwest of the retirement home.

sets.title: Roads and streets
sets.place: Granford: High Street, Station Road and School Road
sets.focus: Which side of the road, and how roads meet.

words.meaning: facing it on the other side of a road or space
on the other side of the road
on the same side of the road, not across it
you reach this first, then the other place
where two or more roads meet
a road that is closed at one end — you can't go through
starts from (branches off) another road

sentences.text: The chemist is opposite a supermarket.
They are going to build new houses across the road from the school at point G.
There is a supermarket on the same side of the road as the library.
Walk west along High Street and you'll pass the library before you get to the junction with Station Road.

The bank is on a dead end road that leads off the High Street.

sets.title: Around a town centre
sets.focus: Curves in the road, things side by side, and keeping going.

words.meaning: a curve in a road or river
a little after something, once you have gone by it

joined to each other, sharing a wall
keep going forward in the same direction

sentences.text: The school is situated on a bend in the dual carriageway.
The bus station is on the right just past the shopping centre.
The town centre has a pedestrian walkway running alongside a row of adjoining shops.
The town centre has a pedestrian walkway running alongside a row of adjoining shops.
After passing the school on your right, carry straight on and you'll see the park on your left around the next bend.
